issue.title: sase-core's icon-field requirement for ArtifactRefProviderSpecWire breaks sase's provider specs (unreleased feature ahead of Python support)
issue.description:
sase-core commit 4f8c99e ('feat(artifact-ref): require icon field in provider ref spec wire'), which sits on sase-core's master after the 0.26.7 release tag (8bb76d1) and before commit 87e4a4f (needed for AGENT_SCAN_WIRE_SCHEMA_VERSION=6, added on sase's side in sase commit dc9da5576), makes the Rust artifact_ref_provider_spec_validate binding reject every ArtifactRefProviderSpecWire dict lacking an 'icon' field. sase's Python side has not been updated to supply 'icon' anywhere a provider spec is built: src/sase/artifact_providers/_builtin.py's builtin_plan_ref_provider_spec(), src/sase/sidecar_ref_config.py's _default_document_spec(), and multiple test fixtures across the suite.

REPRODUCTION (2026-08-13): with sase at master (dc9da5576) and sase-core rebased to its tip (87e4a4f, chronologically after the icon commit), 'just check''s test-scoped run failed 22 tests, all with 'ValueError: spec is not a valid ArtifactRefProviderSpecWire dict: missing field icon': tests/test_artifact_provider_registry.py (4 nodes, including completely generic registry-fixture specs unrelated to any real provider), tests/test_sidecar_ref_config.py (7 nodes), tests/doctor/test_checks_config_repos.py (6 nodes), tests/agents_sync/test_referenced_by_planning.py, and tests/artifact_refs/test_context.py. Checking sase-core back out to 8bb76d1 (last commit before the icon requirement, still inside the sase-core-rs>=0.26.6,<0.27.0 floor) made all 22 failures disappear with no other changes.

IMPACT: any workspace whose sase-core linked checkout advances past the icon-field commit -- including via the documented 'sase repo open sase-core' recovery path that 'just install' itself recommends when it detects a stale wire schema -- will deterministically break the entire artifact-ref provider-spec validation surface, not just artifact refs specifically opted into icons.

SCOPE: add an 'icon' field (with a sensible default such as an empty string, or whatever default sase-core's Rust side treats as 'no icon') to builtin_plan_ref_provider_spec() and _default_document_spec(), and update any inline test-fixture provider specs the new requirement now rejects, so sase's Python side is coordinated with sase-core's icon-field feature before that feature reaches a released sase-core-rs version.
